title: The Milky Way Shines on Paranal
caption: The Milky Way over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The glowing plane of the Milky Way, seen edge-on and laced with bands of dust and dark gas, slices across the night sky above ESO's facilities on Mount Paranal in Chile's Atacama Desert. In the lower right corner hangs the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of our galaxy's satellites, above the Residencia, where staff and visitors stay.

The three-minute exposure also caught some action on the ground. At left, a car pauses, parking lights glowing, to drop off a passenger. Even under the Milky Way's glow the high desert stays quite dark, so the passenger carries a small flashlight along the path to the Residencia's underground entrance ramp, and its light traces a bright squiggle. At lower right, the Residencia's rooftop glass dome mirrors the starry sky.
Paranal hosts the Very Large Telescope (VLT), which ESO describes as the world's most advanced ground-based astronomical observatory.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based photograph taken with a digital camera and a three-minute exposure, credited to B. Fugate (FASORtronics)/ESO. The source does not publish colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Three minutes of exposure gathers far more light than the eye, which is why the Milky Way looks so bright here while the desert actually stayed quite dark, and why the moving flashlight became a squiggly line.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: When this picture was published, two new survey telescopes were being built at Paranal, VISTA (the Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy) and the VLT Survey Telescope (VST). Both were expected to begin work in the 2009-2010 timeframe.
alt: The Milky Way slicing across a dark sky over desert buildings, with a vehicle's lights at left, a squiggly flashlight trail, a glass dome reflecting stars and a fuzzy patch at lower right.
